claims.text: W-V-Ta-Ti-Cr is a refractory multi-principal-element alloy system that can be deposited by laser cladding on 42-CrMo steel.
A linear energy density of 2.5–3.0 J/mm will maintain a single BCC solid solution during laser cladding of W-V-Ta-Ti-Cr.
Cr contents above 15 at.% can be maximized while retaining a single BCC W-V-Ta-Ti-Cr solid solution.
Annealing at 1000–1100 °C for one hour will relieve residual stresses without causing excessive phase decomposition.
Rapid-solidification processing will produce a refined BCC matrix with a high grain-boundary density.
Rapid cooling during laser cladding suppresses diffusion-controlled formation of brittle C14 Laves phases or other intermetallics.
Rapid cooling promotes a homogeneous single-BCC phase.
High Cr content in rapidly solidified W-V-Ta-Ti-Cr will form a dense, continuous, and adherent Cr2O3 scale during high-temperature exposure.
A Cr2O3 scale will impede oxygen ingress and prevent depletion of protective elements from the alloy bulk.
Solid-solution strengthening and grain refinement will increase the hardness of the laser-clad alloy.
Laser-clad W-V-Ta-Ti-Cr will have better high-temperature oxidation resistance than an as-cast counterpart.
Laser-clad W-V-Ta-Ti-Cr will exhibit more than a 20% microhardness increase relative to as-cast material.
The alloy will have room-temperature yield strength above 1500 MPa.
After 100 hours at 950 °C, laser-clad material will have a parabolic oxidation-rate constant more than 50% lower than the as-cast control.
The oxide scale will show no spallation after 100 hours at 950 °C.
Conventionally cast material typically has coarser grains than intensely processed material.
As-cast W-V-Ta-Ti-Cr may contain brittle Laves phases.
As-cast or lower-Cr W-V-Ta-Ti-Cr has inferior oxidation resistance because it forms non-protective oxides or undergoes scale spallation.
The proposed mechanism is valid over a Cr-content window of 10–25 at.%.
Above 25 at.% Cr, the risk of brittle sigma or Laves-phase formation increases significantly.

contradictions.description: The intervention specifies laser cladding, which ordinarily requires formation of a molten pool, while the boundary states that the processing temperature must remain below the alloy melting point. This is internally inconsistent unless the boundary is intended to apply only to the post-process anneal.
